title.en: Global Recognition, Crop Diversity and Scientific Assessment
title.te: ప్రపంచ గుర్తింపులు, పంటల వైవిధ్యం, శాస్త్రీయ అంచనాలు

paragraphs.en: Global biodiversity institutions do not all perform the same function. UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme recognises places where conservation, sustainable development and scientific learning are pursued together. The World Heritage Convention identifies properties of Outstanding Universal Value. The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture governs cooperation over crop diversity, while IPBES assesses scientific knowledge for policymakers. Recognition, treaty obligations and scientific assessment must therefore be studied separately.
paragraphs.te: ప్రపంచ స్థాయిలో పనిచేసే biodiversity institutions అన్నీ ఒకే పని చేయవు. UNESCO యొక్క Man and the Biosphere Programme, conservationతో పాటు sustainable development, research, educationను కలిపి అమలు చేసే ప్రాంతాలను గుర్తిస్తుంది. World Heritage Convention, Outstanding Universal Value ఉన్న ప్రదేశాలను గుర్తిస్తుంది. International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture పంటల genetic diversityపై దేశాల సహకారానికి framework ఇస్తుంది. IPBES మాత్రం policymakers కోసం scientific evidenceను అంచనా వేస్తుంది. కాబట్టి recognition, treaty obligation, scientific assessment — ఈ మూడింటిని ఒకటిగా చూడకూడదు.

paragraphs.en: UNESCO launched the Man and the Biosphere Programme in 1971. A biosphere reserve performs three connected functions: conserving biodiversity, supporting sustainable development, and providing logistic support through research, monitoring, education and training. Its core zone gives priority to long-term conservation. Activities compatible with conservation may occur in the buffer zone, while the transition zone supports cooperation and sustainable livelihoods. A biosphere reserve declared by India does not automatically enter UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves; India must nominate it and UNESCO must approve it. After Cold Desert joined the network in 2025, India had 18 domestically designated biosphere reserves, of which 13 were in the UNESCO network. These totals must always be quoted with their reference year.
paragraphs.te: UNESCO 1971లో Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programmeను ప్రారంభించింది. ఒక biosphere reserveకు మూడు ముఖ్యమైన functions ఉంటాయి: biodiversity conservation, sustainable development, research–monitoring–education–trainingకు logistic support. Core zoneలో long-term conservationకు మొదటి ప్రాధాన్యం ఉంటుంది. Buffer zoneలో conservationకు అనుకూలమైన activities చేయవచ్చు. Transition zoneలో స్థానిక ప్రజల భాగస్వామ్యంతో sustainable livelihoodsను ప్రోత్సహిస్తారు. భారతదేశం ఒక ప్రాంతాన్ని biosphere reserveగా ప్రకటించినంత మాత్రాన అది UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reservesలో చేరదు. భారత్ దాన్ని విడిగా nominate చేయాలి; UNESCO approve చేయాలి. Cold Desert 2025లో UNESCO networkలో చేరిన తరువాత, భారత్‌లో 18 domestic biosphere reserves ఉండగా వాటిలో 13 UNESCO networkలో ఉన్నాయి. ఈ సంఖ్యలను yearతో కలిపి మాత్రమే గుర్తుంచుకోవాలి.

paragraphs.en: Nilgiri, designated in 1986, was India's first biosphere reserve and is in UNESCO's World Network. Seshachalam Hills in Andhra Pradesh was designated domestically in 2010 but is not in that network. Manas National Park has World Heritage recognition, but this does not make Manas Biosphere Reserve a member of the UNESCO biosphere-reserve network. These examples show that domestic biosphere-reserve status, World Heritage status and WNBR membership are separate recognitions. India's biosphere-reserve programme does not by itself create a new statutory protected-area category; legal restrictions within its zones arise from the wildlife, forest or environmental law applicable to the component area.
paragraphs.te: 1986లో ప్రకటించిన Nilgiri, భారతదేశపు తొలి biosphere reserve; ఇది UNESCO World Networkలో కూడా ఉంది. ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌లోని Seshachalam Hillsను 2010లో domestic biosphere reserveగా ప్రకటించారు; కానీ అది UNESCO networkలో లేదు. Manas National Parkకు World Heritage recognition ఉంది; అయినా Manas Biosphere Reserve UNESCO biosphere-reserve networkలో member కాదు. అంటే domestic biosphere reserve status, World Heritage status, WNBR membership మూడు వేర్వేరు recognitions. భారత biosphere-reserve programme స్వయంగా కొత్త statutory protected-area categoryను సృష్టించదు. దాని zonesలో అమలయ్యే legal restrictions, ఆ ప్రాంతానికి వర్తించే wildlife, forest లేదా environmental law నుంచి వస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: The 1972 World Heritage Convention covers cultural, natural and mixed properties. A property must demonstrate Outstanding Universal Value, satisfy at least one of ten selection criteria, and meet protection and management requirements. Criteria (i) to (vi) concern cultural values; criteria (vii) to (x) concern natural values. A mixed property satisfies at least one cultural and one natural criterion. The World Heritage Committee does not examine a nomination unless the property is already on the State Party's Tentative List. World Heritage recognition is therefore different from biosphere-reserve recognition in both purpose and procedure.
paragraphs.te: 1972 World Heritage Conventionలో cultural, natural, mixed properties ఉంటాయి. World Heritage Listలో చేరాలంటే ఒక propertyకు Outstanding Universal Value ఉండాలి; పది selection criteriaలో కనీసం ఒకటి satisfy చేయాలి; protection, management requirementsను కూడా meet చేయాలి. Criteria (i) నుంచి (vi) వరకు cultural valuesకు, (vii) నుంచి (x) వరకు natural valuesకు సంబంధించినవి. కనీసం ఒక cultural criterion, ఒక natural criterion satisfy చేస్తే దాన్ని mixed property అంటారు. ఒక property ముందుగా ఆ దేశపు Tentative Listలో లేకపోతే World Heritage Committee దాని nominationను పరిశీలించదు. అందువల్ల World Heritage recognition, biosphere-reserve recognition — purposeలోనూ procedureలోనూ వేర్వేరు.

paragraphs.en: The FAO Conference adopted the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture in 2001, and it entered into force on 29 June 2004. Its Multilateral System provides facilitated access and benefit-sharing for 64 food crops and forages listed in Annex I through a Standard Material Transfer Agreement. The Treaty also recognises Farmers' Rights, including the protection of traditional knowledge, participation in benefit-sharing and participation in relevant decision-making; responsibility for implementing those rights rests with national governments under national law.
paragraphs.te: FAO Conference, International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agricultureను 2001లో adopt చేసింది. ఇది 29 June 2004న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. దీని Multilateral System, Annex Iలో ఉన్న 64 food crops and foragesకు facilitated access, benefit-sharingను Standard Material Transfer Agreement ద్వారా అందిస్తుంది. ఈ Treaty, Farmers' Rightsను కూడా గుర్తిస్తుంది. Traditional knowledgeను కాపాడటం, benefitsలో భాగస్వామ్యం, సంబంధిత decision-makingలో participation వీటిలో ముఖ్యమైనవి. అయితే ఈ rightsను national law ప్రకారం అమలు చేయాల్సిన బాధ్యత ఆయా national governmentsదే.

paragraphs.en: IPBES was established in 2012 as an independent intergovernmental science-policy body. It reviews available knowledge on biodiversity and ecosystem services and presents assessments to policymakers. It does not make treaties, create protected areas or enforce binding targets. Its 2019 Global Assessment estimated that about one million animal and plant species faced extinction threat, many within decades. The comparison with the IPCC is useful only to understand its assessment role: IPBES focuses on biodiversity, whereas the IPCC focuses on climate change.
paragraphs.te: IPBES 2012లో ఏర్పడిన independent intergovernmental science-policy body. Biodiversity, ecosystem servicesపై ఉన్న knowledgeను review చేసి policymakersకు assessments అందిస్తుంది. ఇది treatiesను తయారు చేయదు; protected areasను ప్రకటించదు; binding targetsను enforce చేయదు. దీని 2019 Global Assessment ప్రకారం, సుమారు one million animal and plant species extinction threatను ఎదుర్కొంటున్నాయి; వాటిలో చాలా species కొన్ని decadesలోనే ప్రమాదాన్ని ఎదుర్కొనవచ్చు. IPCCతో comparison, assessment roleను అర్థం చేసుకోవడానికి మాత్రమే ఉపయోగపడుతుంది: IPBES biodiversityపై, IPCC climate changeపై దృష్టి పెడతాయి.

exam_distinctions: MAB biosphere reserve: conservation + sustainable development + research/learning.
World Heritage property: Outstanding Universal Value under the 1972 Convention.
Domestic biosphere reserve status does not automatically create WNBR membership.
World Heritage recognition of a national park does not create WNBR membership for a biosphere reserve.
ITPGRFA: crop genetic resources, Multilateral System and Farmers' Rights.
IPBES: scientific assessment body, not a treaty regulator.

title.en: India's International Commitments, Finance and Reporting
title.te: భారత అంతర్జాతీయ కట్టుబాట్లు, ఆర్థిక వ్యవస్థలు, నివేదికలు

paragraphs.en: An international biodiversity commitment does not implement itself within India. The global commitment is translated into national targets, laws, institutions, programmes, budgets and reports. Under the Convention on Biological Diversity, India's implementation chain can be read as: the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework at the global level; India's updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan at the national level; and implementation through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards or Union Territory Biodiversity Councils, and local Biodiversity Management Committees.
paragraphs.te: ఒక international biodiversity commitment భారతదేశంలో తనంతట తానే అమలుకాదు. Global commitmentను national targets, laws, institutions, programmes, budgets, reports ద్వారా అమలులోకి తీసుకువస్తారు. Convention on Biological Diversity విషయంలో ఈ chainను ఇలా గుర్తుంచుకోవచ్చు: global levelలో Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework; national levelలో India's updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan; implementationలో Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards లేదా Union Territory Biodiversity Councils, local Biodiversity Management Committees.

paragraphs.en: India released its updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan for 2024–2030 at CBD COP16 in October 2024. It is aligned with the four goals and 23 targets of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and sets 23 National Biodiversity Targets suited to India's circumstances. The plan connects conservation with ecosystem restoration, species recovery, sustainable use, benefit-sharing, pollution control, invasive-species management and the protection of terrestrial, wetland, coastal and marine ecosystems. A global target and India's national target may point in the same direction, but they should not be treated as identical legal provisions.
paragraphs.te: CBD COP16 సందర్భంగా October 2024లో India తన updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2024–2030ను విడుదల చేసింది. ఇది Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Frameworkలోని four goals, 23 targetsకు అనుగుణంగా ఉండి, భారత పరిస్థితులకు సరిపోయే 23 National Biodiversity Targetsను నిర్దేశించింది. Ecosystem restoration, species recovery, sustainable use, benefit-sharing, pollution control, invasive-species management, terrestrial–wetland–coastal–marine ecosystems protectionను ఈ plan కలిపి చూస్తుంది. Global target, India's national target ఒకే దిశలో ఉండవచ్చు; కానీ రెండింటినీ ఒకే legal provisionగా భావించకూడదు.

paragraphs.en: National reports show how implementation is progressing. India submitted its Seventh National Report to the CBD on 26 February 2026 under Article 26 of the Convention. The report uses 142 national indicators mapped to the 23 National Biodiversity Targets. India also submitted its first National Report on implementation of the Nagoya Protocol on 27 February 2026 under Article 29 of that Protocol. The two reports have different legal bases and subjects: the CBD report covers the wider biodiversity framework, while the Nagoya report focuses on access and benefit-sharing.
paragraphs.te: National reports ద్వారా implementation ఎంతవరకు ముందుకు వెళ్లిందో తెలియజేస్తారు. CBD Article 26 ప్రకారం India తన Seventh National Reportను 26 February 2026న submit చేసింది. ఇందులో 23 National Biodiversity Targetsకు map చేసిన 142 national indicatorsను ఉపయోగించారు. Nagoya Protocol implementationపై India's first National Reportను, ఆ Protocolలోని Article 29 ప్రకారం, 27 February 2026న submit చేశారు. ఈ రెండు reportsకు legal basis, subject వేరు. CBD report మొత్తం biodiversity frameworkను పరిశీలిస్తుంది; Nagoya report access and benefit-sharingపై focus చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: The BBNJ Agreement concerns the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. It was adopted on 19 June 2023 and entered into force on 17 January 2026, 120 days after deposit of the sixtieth instrument as provided in Article 68. It is the third implementing agreement under UNCLOS, not a protocol under the CBD. Its four main subjects are marine genetic resources and fair and equitable benefit-sharing; area-based management tools, including marine protected areas; environmental impact assessments; and capacity-building with transfer of marine technology. It must be applied consistently with UNCLOS and without undermining relevant legal instruments, frameworks and bodies.
paragraphs.te: National jurisdictionకు బయట ఉన్న marine biodiversity conservation, sustainable useకు సంబంధించిన ఒప్పందమే BBNJ Agreement. ఇది 19 June 2023న adopt అయింది. Article 68 ప్రకారం 60వ instrument deposit చేసిన 120 రోజుల తరువాత, 17 January 2026న అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. ఇది UNCLOS కింద third implementing agreement; CBD protocol కాదు. దీనిలో నాలుగు ప్రధాన subjects ఉన్నాయి: marine genetic resources, fair and equitable benefit-sharing; marine protected areas సహా area-based management tools; environmental impact assessments; capacity-building, transfer of marine technology. దీన్ని UNCLOSకు అనుగుణంగా, సంబంధిత legal instruments, frameworks, bodiesను బలహీనపరచకుండా అమలు చేయాలి.

paragraphs.en: Areas beyond national jurisdiction contain two legally distinct spaces: the high seas, meaning the water column beyond national jurisdiction, and 'the Area', meaning the seabed, ocean floor and subsoil beyond national jurisdiction. The BBNJ Agreement can help countries coordinate the marine component of the 30×30 conservation goal, but it does not itself convert the Kunming–Montreal target into a BBNJ treaty obligation. India signed the BBNJ Agreement on 25 September 2024. In the United Nations Treaty Collection record checked for this draft, India had signed but had not deposited an instrument of ratification. Signature, ratification and becoming a Party are separate legal stages, so India's status must be rechecked before publication or an examination.
paragraphs.te: Areas beyond national jurisdictionలో రెండు legally distinct spaces ఉంటాయి. National jurisdictionకు బయట ఉన్న water columnను high seas అంటారు. అక్కడి seabed, ocean floor, subsoilను ‘the Area’ అంటారు. 30 × 30 conservation goalలోని marine భాగాన్ని అమలు చేయడానికి BBNJ Agreement coordinationకు సహాయపడగలదు; కానీ Kunming–Montreal targetను అది తనంతట తానే BBNJ treaty obligationగా మార్చదు. India 25 September 2024న BBNJ Agreementపై sign చేసింది. ఈ draft కోసం పరిశీలించిన United Nations Treaty Collection recordలో India signature మాత్రమే ఉంది; ratification instrument deposit చేసినట్టు నమోదు లేదు. Signature, ratification, Party కావడం మూడు వేర్వేరు legal stages. కాబట్టి publication లేదా examinationకు ముందు India's current statusను మళ్లీ verify చేయాలి.

paragraphs.en: The Global Environment Facility is a financing partnership, not a convention and not a United Nations specialised agency. The World Bank acts as its Trustee. Under the guidance of the respective Conference of the Parties, the GEF serves as a financial mechanism for several environmental agreements. Under Article 52 of the BBNJ Agreement, its financial mechanism includes a voluntary trust fund, a special fund and the GEF Trust Fund. These funds perform related but different functions and should not be treated as one fund.
paragraphs.te: Global Environment Facility (GEF) ఒక financing partnership. ఇది convention కాదు; United Nations specialised agency కూడా కాదు. World Bank దీనికి Trusteeగా పనిచేస్తుంది. సంబంధిత Conference of the Parties ఇచ్చే guidance ప్రకారం, GEF అనేక environmental agreementsకు financial mechanismగా సేవలందిస్తుంది. BBNJ Agreement Article 52 ప్రకారం, దాని financial mechanismలో voluntary trust fund, special fund, GEF Trust Fund ఉంటాయి. ఇవి పరస్పరం సంబంధం ఉన్నా, ఒకే fund కాదు; వాటి functions వేర్వేరు.

paragraphs.en: The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF) is a separate trust fund in the GEF family that supports implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. It complements rather than replaces the main GEF Trust Fund and can receive public, private and philanthropic contributions. The Cali Fund serves a different purpose: it is the multilateral benefit-sharing mechanism for the use of digital sequence information on genetic resources. It was launched on 25 February 2025, expects contributions from eligible large commercial users of DSI, and allocates at least 50 per cent of its resources to the self-identified needs of Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
paragraphs.te: Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF), GEF familyలోని separate trust fund. Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework implementationకు ఇది support ఇస్తుంది. Main GEF Trust Fundను ఇది replace చేయదు; దానికి అదనంగా పనిచేస్తుంది. Public, private, philanthropic sources నుంచి contributions తీసుకోగలదు. Cali Fund పని వేరు. Genetic resourcesకు సంబంధించిన Digital Sequence Information (DSI) వినియోగం వల్ల వచ్చే benefitsను పంచుకునే multilateral mechanism ఇది. 25 February 2025న launch అయింది. Eligible large commercial DSI users నుంచి contributionsను ఆశిస్తుంది. దీని resourcesలో కనీసం 50 per centను Indigenous Peoples and local communities తమకు అవసరమని స్వయంగా గుర్తించిన కార్యక్రమాలకు కేటాయించాలి.

paragraphs.en: The Nagoya Protocol and the BBNJ Agreement use different benefit-sharing models. Under the Nagoya Protocol, access to physical genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge is generally arranged between a provider and a user in accordance with applicable domestic law, using prior informed consent and mutually agreed terms where required. The BBNJ Agreement creates a multilateral system for marine genetic resources and associated digital sequence information collected or generated in areas beyond national jurisdiction, because there is no single provider State for those areas. The Cali Fund is again different: it deals with benefit-sharing from the commercial use of DSI on genetic resources under the CBD system.
paragraphs.te: Nagoya Protocol, BBNJ Agreementలో benefit-sharing models వేర్వేరు. Nagoya Protocol కింద physical genetic resources, associated traditional knowledgeకు access సాధారణంగా provider–user మధ్య, వర్తించే domestic law ప్రకారం ఏర్పాటు అవుతుంది. అవసరమైన సందర్భాల్లో Prior Informed Consent (PIC), Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT)ను ఉపయోగిస్తారు. BBNJ Agreement మాత్రం national jurisdictionకు బయట సేకరించిన marine genetic resources, వాటికి సంబంధించిన Digital Sequence Information కోసం multilateral systemను ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుంది; అక్కడ ఒకే provider State ఉండదు. Cali Fund మరో విధమైన mechanism. ఇది CBD system కింద genetic resourcesకు సంబంధించిన DSI commercial use నుంచి వచ్చే benefit-sharingపై పనిచేస్తుంది.

exam_distinctions: KMGBF: global framework; NBSAP: India's national implementation roadmap.
CBD Seventh National Report: wider biodiversity implementation; Nagoya report: access and benefit-sharing implementation.
BBNJ: UNCLOS implementing agreement, not a CBD protocol.
Signature does not equal ratification or Party status.
GEF: financing partnership; GBFF: KMGBF-focused trust fund; Cali Fund: DSI benefit-sharing mechanism.
Nagoya ABS is generally provider–user based; BBNJ marine genetic-resource benefit-sharing is multilateral.
